questions.q:
Let $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$ be the function defined by
$f(x)= \begin{cases}x^2-4 x-5 & \text { if } x \geq 1, \\ 2 x & \text { if } x \lt 1 .\end{cases}$

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: $\quad f$ is onto but not one-one
$\quad f$ is one-one but not onto
$\quad f$ is neither one-one nor onto

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$ be a strictly decreasing function with $|f(t)| \lt \pi / 2$ for all $t \in \mathbf{R}$. Let $g:[0, \pi] \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$ be a function defined by $g(t)=\sin (f(t))$. Which one of the following statements is Correct?
options: $g$ is decreasing on $(0, \pi / 2)$ and increasing on $(\pi / 2, \pi)$.
$g$ is increasing on $(0, \pi / 2)$ and decreasing on $(\pi / 2, \pi)$.
